context: Mrs. Mori and Sachiko share autumn childhood memories.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.style: Warm, curious opening. Soft, genuine tone—not performing kindness but feeling it. Leans in slightly. Inviting her to share without pressure.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.style: Quiet certainty, almost wistful. Settles into the word 'favorite' with genuine tenderness. No rush. The voice of someone looking back with gratitude.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: 昔の思い出、たくさん、ある。
lines.en: I have so many old memories from those days.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost dreaming aloud. Soft pace, nostalgic undertone. Not sad—grateful. A small smile threading through the words.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: When I was little, I'd pick chestnuts.
lines.style: Gentle reminiscence, eyes distant. Speaks as if seeing it happen again. Warm, unhurried. The tenderness of someone who loved those days.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: 懐かしい！柿も、よく食べた。
lines.en: How nostalgic! I ate persimmons so much back then too.
lines.style: Bright recognition—a small spark of shared memory. Warm excitement, but grounded. Not loud, just genuinely delighted to have found this common ground.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: We have the same autumn memories together.
lines.style: Soft realization, almost wondering. Voice becomes deeper with meaning. Settles on 'together' with quiet weight. The recognition of something precious.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.style: Closing gently, with finality that feels like a gift. Barely audible trailing breath. No wistfulness—just quiet gratitude for what was shared. Almost a benediction.
